core_obligations: Choose bounded below representatives (proof lines 18949-18960): write H^i(E) = 0 for i >= a and H^j(K) = 0 for j >= b, represent K by the bounded below complex K^bullet = tau_{>= b-1}L^bullet of torsion free Z-modules (using a K-flat resolution and the last-one-flat criterion, valid since Z has global dimension one), and represent E by a bounded below complex E^bullet, so that E tensor^L_Z underline K is represented by Tot(E^bullet tensor_Z underline K^bullet).

Run the truncation reductions (proof lines 18961-18985): using the truncation triangles of K^bullet and the displayed vanishing of H^n of both Tot(E^bullet tensor_Z sigma_{>=-a+n+1}underline K^bullet) and R Gamma(X, E) tensor^L_Z sigma_{>=-a+n+1}K^bullet, reduce first to K^bullet a bounded complex of flat Z-modules and then to K^bullet a single flat Z-module in one degree; the same argument with the stupid truncations of E^bullet reduces further to E a single abelian sheaf.

Finish on a flat module (proof lines 18986-18998): it remains to check H^n(X, E tensor_Z underline M) = H^n(X, E) tensor_Z M for a flat Z-module M, where one writes M as a filtered colimit of finite free Z-modules by Lazard's theorem, applies the colimit theorem to reduce to M finite free, and in that case the identity is the trivial one.
proof_roadmap: Replace K by a bounded below complex of torsion free Z-modules and E by a bounded below complex.
Reduce by the truncation triangles to K a single flat Z-module and E a single abelian sheaf.
Write the flat module as a filtered colimit of finite free modules (Lazard) and apply the colimit theorem, leaving the trivial finite free case.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the global sections of E tensor^L_Z underline K as R Gamma(X, E) tensor^L_Z K for a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme X (statement lines 18937-18946). The proof (proof lines 18948-18998) is a sequence of reductions: a torsion free bounded below representative of K, truncation triangles reducing K to a single flat module and E to a single sheaf, and then Lazard's theorem plus the colimit theorem reducing the flat module to a finite free one, where the identity is trivial. H2: three explicit reduction steps, each written out.
